faq.q: How much does Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers charge?
faq.a: Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers publishes a free initial consultation. It publishes material in Spanish.

faq.q: Where does Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers have offices?
faq.a: Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers publishes four offices, among them San Antonio, Austin and Laredo. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers?
faq.a: Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers names 18 attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: Texas does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.q: Are the case results Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers publishes verified?
faq.a: No. Texas Law Guns, Injury & Accident Lawyers publishes 21 case results with amounts on its own site. We counted them and we did not confirm them: the figures are the firm's. Pillar B scores whether a firm publishes outcomes and discloses them properly, including whether a prior-results disclaimer appears beside them, not whether the amounts are right. Past results do not predict another case.
